Finding Title: Logout does not invalidate sessions on the server
Affected Component: Auth.js Credentials JWT sign-out and shared protected-session verification
Description: The configured JWT sign-out clears the browser cookie and records no server-side revocation for that session. The inspected backend verifies JWT validity and the active account state. The ordinary logout sample removed the cookie and the protected API returned 401 for that signed-out client. The 3302 Playwright follow-up confirmed ordinary sign-out. Acceptance of the original JWT after logout was not tested. HT-11 is a related source-based Fail for the re-authentication trigger. The protected-route outcome for the superseded session remains unobserved. The 21 November follow-up corroborated ordinary logout and concurrent sessions from independent sign-ins. Prior-session acceptance after actual replacement or logout remains unobserved.
Evidence Reference: ../evidence/phase-3/HT-12-evidence.md | ../evidence/phase-3/observations.json (http.logout and jwtExpiry) | ../evidence/supplementary/2026-11-20/network/clone-browser-observations.json (ordinary logout only, replay untested) | ../evidence/supplementary/2026-11-21/criterion-recheck/review.md (HT-11 source Fail and separate dynamic limitation) | ../evidence/supplementary/2026-11-21/remaining-evidence/working-paper.md | ../evidence/supplementary/2026-11-21/remaining-evidence/final-evidence-disposition.md | ../evidence/supplementary/2026-11-21/final-dynamic-validation/evidence-index.md | ../evidence/supplementary/2026-11-21/ht11-context-reassessment.md
Security Impact: Someone already in possession of a valid session artifact who can reach the lab could retain access allowed by that role after logout. A privileged session could permit management actions. No possession, misuse or retained access by another party was observed.
Recommended Remediation: Add durable per-session state keyed by a stable server-issued session ID. Check it consistently during verification and require durable revocation before reporting logout success.
Verification Method After Remediation: Use isolated synthetic integration tests to confirm active, revoked and expired server states, renewal behavior and persistence. Corroborate with ordinary authorized logout and redacted UI/API results.
Expected Criterion: Logout or expiry makes a terminated session unusable at the backend.

Finding Title: Admin contact search includes an email in a request URL
Affected Component: Admin people search client, entity list GET handler and Prisma user search
Description: Source constructs and accepts a free-text query parameter that can match an email. The sampled admin search put a synthetic teacher email into the request query and returned the matching record. The 3302 Playwright follow-up independently observed HTTP 200 with the exact synthetic email in the URL and one matching teacher.
Security Impact: A contact value can be copied into browser network captures or into server, proxy or observability records that retain URLs. Actual secondary retention and disclosure were unverified. The evidenced field was contact information.
Recommended Remediation: Move free-text contact searches into a validated POST body on a dedicated read-only admin route. Retire legacy free-text URL input and suppress sensitive data in logs, traces and caches.
Verification Method After Remediation: Perform ordinary authorized search with a synthetic marker and verify matches and body-only placement. Check server authorization, legacy handling, cache policy, and marker absence from URLs and available local logs or traces.
Expected Criterion: Keep sensitive input out of request URLs and use the request body or headers.

Affected Component: Authentication documentation and sign-in control design
Description: The available README names a hashed in-memory limiter and omits its effective configuration, reset and safeguards against malicious account lockout. No other supplied application document fills the gap. The Project Owner subsequently approved an operating baseline for the follow-up. The approved-baseline implementation comparison found a threshold and timing mismatch under HT-07. The historical documentation finding remains open.
Security Impact: Incomplete guidance can lead to inconsistent maintenance or weak verification of sign-in protection. The reviewed evidence does not establish a successful attack or a failed implementation.
Recommended Remediation: Maintain an approved, versioned credential-abuse policy documenting the defenses, settings, reset and protection against malicious lockout.
Verification Method After Remediation: Review policy coverage and version, then compare the documented settings with actual configuration. Assess implementation behavior separately under HT-07.
Expected Criterion: Document the defenses against credential abuse, their configuration and how malicious lockout is prevented.

Affected Component: Application role permissions and student or group access rules
Description: The README summarizes server role and ownership checks. Available application documentation leaves function permissions and resource attributes for sampled records incomplete.
Security Impact: Future access changes could be inconsistent across roles or expose a bounded set of school records. Sampled runtime authorization passed.
Recommended Remediation: Maintain an approved authorization policy and role-permission matrix covering functions, resources, relationships, lifecycle state, denials and exceptions.
Verification Method After Remediation: Inspect the approved policy for coverage and compare representative rules with backend enforcement under the defined scope.
Expected Criterion: Document function-level and data-specific authorization rules based on permissions and resource attributes.
